summary: A 1949 Aermotor MC-99 steel lookout in the Lincoln National Forest, Guadalupe Ranger District, built on a site used for fire detection since 1910.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-99 steel tower, 48 ft high (the top 48 ft of a 90 ft U.S. Army surplus tower), with a 7 x 7 ft steel cab; CCC observer's cabin and shed beside it

access.note: Listed by the Forest Service as an open observation site. The register marks the lookout as available for rental. No current booking listing was found.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Lincoln National Forest, Guadalupe Ranger District)

events.note: Fire detection begins at the site using two tall pine trees with ladders and platforms
Surplus U.S. Army tower received and erected; original 90 ft, top 48 ft used
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, August 30, 2015
Forest Service proposed a $65 per night fee for overnight rental of the lookout and cabin; neither was yet open for overnight use
Lookout complex nominated to the National Register and in final transmittal for listing, per the 2020 chapter report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Forest Service date the present CCC cabin to the late 1930s. The 2020 chapter report says late 1939. The 1949 tower date agrees across all sources.

The register marks the lookout as available for rental, and a 2020 report said it would join the cabin rental program once running. A 2016 notice proposed a fee. No current booking listing was found, so rental status is unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced across the register, the Forest Service and the 2016 Federal Register notice. Open items: the CCC cabin date (late 1930s per NHLR and FS, late 1939 per the 2020 chapter report); current rental status (register says available, no booking listing found; the 2016 fee was a proposal, and adoption was not confirmed); whether the complex has been listed on the National Register (2020 report says nominated, final transmittal, listing not confirmed in later sources); climbability of the tower, which no source states. The record fields checked (county Eddy, elevation 2123.8 m, built 1949, public access, standing) match the register; no corrections proposed. The Flickr album and the 2012 photo credit by Mark Gutzman were noted but not added as photos because no image URLs were fetched.
